data.name: Amogha
data.gender_notes: Amogha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Amogha is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘amoga’, which means ‘undefeated’, ‘invincible’, or ‘immeasurable’. This name is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and carries a strong spiritual connotation, symbolizing courage, determination, and the power to overcome challenges. The name Amogha carries the meaning “Undefeated, Invincible” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amogha usually hope their child will grow to embody undefeated, invincible and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodying the power of invincibility and courage
data.etymology: Amogha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Undefeated, Invincible.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amogha total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Amogha holds a significant cultural impact within Hindu communities, as it is the name of various gods and deities believed to possess immense power and invincibility. One such deity is Lord Amoghapashana, who is worshipped for granting success, prosperity, and fulfillment of desires. The name also resonates with the heroic tales of such figures as Bhima from the Mahabharata, known as Amogha-veerya, meaning 'Amogha in Valor'.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Amogha carries a deep inspirational meaning, symbolizing invincibility and the strength to overcome adversity. It reminds us of the power of our inner resources and the determination to continue moving forward despite challenges. The name serves as a constant reminder of our inherent bravery and the strength to face any situation with unwavering courage. Furthermore, it is believed that the name Amogha bestows its bearer with the blessings of the gods and the protection from harm, providing a sense of spiritual security and confidence.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amogha: Unfailing, Immutable, Infallible. The name signifies one who is free from all obstacles and failures in their endeavors. It is a symbol of unwavering faith and resilience, inspiring confidence and success in all undertakings.

historical_references.reference: Amoghavarsha I, the Chalukya king (572-642 CE) is also popularly known as Amogha. He ruled over the southern Indian subcontinent and is remembered for his patronage of art, literature and architecture. He built several temples, including the famous Badami cave temples.

Amoghapasana, a ritual described in Hindu texts, involves offering the five essential elements of nature (air, water, earth, fire and ether) to the deity, seeking his/her blessings. The name 'Amogha' in this context refers to the ritual itself, meaning 'infallible' or 'unfailing' as the offering is believed to be accepted without fail.
